solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who's left school educated to destroy

parts.note: an old boy, a former pupil, is abbreviated OB
able to read and write, so literate

explanation.surface: A former pupil uses their schooling for destruction rather than good.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe out completely, leaving no trace, is a straightforward synonym of destroy.

clue.text: Entrance to Circle Line by both ends of Victoria Tube station

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word Victoria are taken

parts.note: a circle looks like the letter O

indicators.note: read as entering, so the following letters go into the circle-and-line pair

explanation.surface: Directions for getting into the London Underground's Circle Line via the Victoria line.
explanation.walkthrough: Circle, Line and Victoria all look like London Underground lines, but they are just letter sources. Oval is a London Underground station named after the Oval, the Test cricket ground beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oval is a stop on the Northern line of the London Underground, known as the Tube.

clue.text: Service computers, etc, in grip of virus, perhaps

indicators.note: held inside, so the computing letters sit within the illness

parts.note: the lurgy is jokey British slang for any unspecified illness, a virus being an example
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

explanation.surface: A church service, or an IT service, is struck down by a computer virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dreaded lurgy' is a British comic name for a vague bug going round, from the radio show The Goon Show.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgy is the set form of public worship, a church service.

clue.text: Half-heartedly comfort child during exam — it could be worth a lot!

definitions.text: it could be worth a lot!

indicators.note: occurring within, so the other pieces are placed inside the exam

parts.note: a test is an exam

indicators.note: the word has a double-letter heart, and losing one of that pair leaves it with half its heart

parts.note: to reassure is to comfort

explanation.surface: A parent half-heartedly consoles a child sitting an exam; the result could be valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes one S from the SS at the centre of REASSURE, giving REASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest full of treasure holds gold and jewels, so its contents could be worth a fortune.

clue.text: Something to eat cooked at supper, cut up

indicators.note: food that is cooked is altered, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word up is cut out of the word supper

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something prepared at supper and then chopped into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes UP out of SUPPER to leave SPER; 'cooked' rearranges AT plus SPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal, something to eat.

clue.text: Second half of cancan coming up — usher, remove that woman causing problem for audience

indicators.note: only the latter part of the doubled word is affected
in a down clue, coming up means reading backwards

parts.note: read as can can, two cans, each a tin

indicators.note: the pronoun is taken out of the word usher

parts.note: her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: At a cancan show an usher is told to remove a woman who is causing trouble for the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The dance name is read as two cans, each a tin; 'Second half of' and 'coming up' turn only the second one, giving NIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinnitus is a ringing in the ears, a problem for anyone listening, here the audience.

clue.text: Northern Irish party's rejected Murphy

indicators.note: turned back, so the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, and the 's gives an S

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish political party turns down someone called Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is informal British and Irish slang for a potato, from its association with Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Murphy and spud are both slang words for a potato.

clue.text: Forecaster relying on manual skills?

parts.note: manual means of the hand, so this is a fortune-teller who reads hands rather than a craftsman

explanation.surface: A predictor who depends on practical, hands-on ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manual skills' suggests craft work; here it is reading the lines of the palm.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm reader foretells a person's future from the lines on their hand.

clue.text: Takes money away from police officers wearing undergarments

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
dressed in, so in
vests are undershirts

explanation.surface: Detectives in their underwear are taking cash away.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinvest is to withdraw capital from a company or venture.

clue.text: An idiot supplying port

parts.note: a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool is the one providing the port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink; it is a harbour city in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian seaport, one of Europe's busiest harbours.

clue.text: Members of the aristocracy gaining billions in swindles

indicators.note: taking on, so the letter is added into the aristocrats

parts.note: nobles are aristocrats
B is the abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: Aristocrats make billions through fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble is British slang meaning to cheat or swindle someone.

clue.text: Outlandish fauns bred to be help to humans

indicators.note: bizarre or strange, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strange fauns are bred to serve mankind.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack animal such as a donkey or ox carries loads, helping people with heavy work.

clue.text: Revival of monkey leaving hospital to get special mention

indicators.note: the letter for hospital departs from the monkey

parts.note: the rhesus is a kind of macaque monkey
a citation is a special mention, as for bravery

explanation.surface: A monkey that recovers and leaves hospital gets an honourable mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Resuscitation is bringing someone back to consciousness, reviving them.

clue.text: Dessert wine is followed by skin complaint

parts.note: blanc is French for white, as in vin blanc, white wine
mange is a skin disease of animals

explanation.surface: Drinking wine leads to a skin rash.
explanation.definitionFit: Blancmange is a sweet set milk pudding, a classic dessert.

clue.text: Pupil of British philosopher gives courses

parts.note: L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the possessive of A. J. Ayer, the British philosopher, is Ayer's

explanation.surface: A student of a British thinker provides lecture courses.
explanation.walkthrough: Pupil seems to belong with the philosopher as a disciple, but it is just L.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses of bricks or stone are layers, horizontal rows in a wall.

clue.text: Provide wording for TV that's refined to describe sex

indicators.note: describing, as in drawing round, means the refined word encloses the other

parts.note: subtle means delicate or refined
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A tasteful way of putting sex into words for a television programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtitle a programme is to add on-screen captions translating or transcribing its speech.

clue.text: Insert cutting digested for detectives

indicators.note: removing, so the word for digested is cut from the longer verb

parts.note: to interpolate is to insert words into a text
ate means consumed and digested

explanation.surface: Inserting a press cutting into a digest for some police detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpol is the international organisation coordinating police and detective work between countries.

clue.text: Perceiving failure to finish the cake?

parts.note: not doing something, so not
putting the icing on is finishing a cake; the word icing

explanation.surface: Spotting that someone forgot to decorate the cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Noticing something is seeing or becoming aware of it, perceiving it.

clue.text: More than one hot drink taken during breakfast is an espresso

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words

explanation.surface: Several hot drinks are consumed at breakfast, including an espresso.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisanes are herbal infusions, hot drinks in the plural.

clue.text: Eliminated, Fulham come in for a bit of stick?

indicators.note: enter, so the club letters go inside the word for eliminated

parts.note: out, as in knocked out of a competition
FFC stands for Fulham Football Club, a London football club

explanation.surface: Fulham, knocked out of the cup, get criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like criticism (British slang 'getting stick'); it is a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed from timber, which could be a bit of stick.

clue.text: Fool gets stuck into wine and starchy food

indicators.note: is placed inside, so the fool goes within the wine

parts.note: cava is Spanish sparkling wine
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool tucks into wine and stodgy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassava is a tropical root vegetable rich in starch, the source of tapioca.

clue.text: Song produced by colonialist on border

parts.note: ants live in colonies, so an ant is jokingly a colonialist
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A song written by an imperialist settler living on the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a rousing song, such as a national one.

clue.text: This person involved in riotous Russian demo — they might be punished

indicators.note: included within, so the word for the speaker goes inside the rearranged letters
unruly and wild, so the letters of these words are scrambled

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves, me

explanation.surface: The setter takes part in an unruly protest in Russia, and the crimes could be punished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' is the setter's usual way of saying ME; 'involved in' puts it in the middle of the shuffled protest letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Misdemeanours are minor offences or wrongdoings, which may incur punishment.

clue.text: Don't go and wander off course — it's not right

indicators.note: the letter for right is not there, so it is dropped

parts.note: to stray is to wander off the path

explanation.surface: An instruction to stay put rather than wander off, since straying is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Stay is the opposite of leave, an instruction not to go.

clue.text: Continuing to lead after having lost bearings?

indicators.note: the verb for leading comes after the phrase for lost bearings

parts.note: no N and S, two compass bearings, so read as NO NS
to top a league table is to lead it

explanation.surface: Carrying on in front even after losing one's way.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO NS: having no N or S, two compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-stop means without a break, continuing all the way.

clue.text: Water source flowed between hotel yard and end of street

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ran, as water runs

indicators.note: the final letter of the word street is taken

explanation.surface: Water ran between a hotel courtyard and the far end of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' places RAN after HYD and before T.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydrant is a street outlet from a water main, a supply for firefighters.

clue.text: Character playing self, perhaps free from anxiety

parts.note: a letter is a character, here E
an actor playing a role appears as it
the same character again, playing itself, so another E

explanation.surface: An actor playing themselves might be relaxed and untroubled.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as E AS E: a letter E playing the part of itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease someone is to relieve them of worry, to free them from anxiety.

clue.text: Three successive letters: AB … why, it sounds like ABC!

parts.note: L, M and N follow one another in the alphabet, spelt out as they are spoken
AB, able seaman, is a sailor, informally a tar

indicators.note: said aloud, the word why is the same as a letter

parts.note: the word why spoken

explanation.surface: A puzzled remark about consecutive letters of the alphabet, A and B.
explanation.walkthrough: L, M, N said out loud gives ELEMEN; ABC also misleads as the start of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something as easy as ABC is elementary, basic and simple.
